law_name: Proposed Law Concerning Age Limits for Social Media
description: Draft law (June 2025) to ban social media for under-15s. 8,000 public consultation submissions with 75% backing electronic age verification. Also raising GDPR consent age to 15. BankID-based verification.

law_name: Social Media (Age Restriction for Users) Bill 2025
description: Original bill banning under-16s withdrawn due to controversy over strict penalties. Lahore High Court petition seeking government response. Revised version expected to lower threshold to 13-14 and shift focus to parental responsibility.

law_name: Multiple Senate bills on social media age restrictions
description: Multiple Senate bills under committee consideration. SB 40 (Lacson) bans up to 18; SB 1735 (Marcos) to 16; SB 595 (Tulfo) to 13; SB 185 (Villar) bans under 12. February 2026 hearing focused on age-appropriate framework.

Digital Affairs Ministry plans measures in 2026 to block children from social media via platform age verification. Civic Coalition/Education Minister bill targeting total restrictions for under-15s; floor vote likely April-May 2026.

law_name: Social Media Digital Majority Law
description: Parliament approved Social Democratic legislation establishing 'digital majority' at 16. Ages 13-15 may access only with verified parental consent. Coalition of Digitally Willing founding member.
Deputy PM announced February 6, 2026 Slovenia is preparing legislation to ban social media for under-15s. Education Ministry leading with expert consultation. Targets TikTok, Snapchat, Instagram.

law_name: Draft White Paper on Online Regulation
description: No government commitment to ban. Draft White Paper emphasizes child protection. SmartphoneFree Childhood SA calling for under-16 ban. SA Human Rights Commission's Social Media Charter is non-binding.

Active debate but no enacted law. Nationwide classroom phone ban from March 2026. Bill to restrict under-16s stalled in National Assembly. New law (effective 2027) prevents platforms from tailoring content to children.

PM Sanchez announced at World Government Summit (February 2026) under-16 social media ban, executive criminal liability, and criminalization of algorithmic manipulation. No legislation passed or introduced yet.
Social Democrats proposed 15-year age limit with mandatory ID verification (October 2025). Unique driver: gangs recruiting children as young as 11 via social media for violent crimes.

85% public support for social media ban. Government will 'discuss comprehensively' in 2026. Federal Commission for Child and Youth Affairs opposes blanket ban. Some cantons have banned phones in schools.

law_name: DES Social Media Age Restriction Draft Rules (2026)
description: DES Ministry drafting rules to bar under-14s from personal social media accounts. Ages 14-16 with parental consent and 2-hour daily caps. Platform executives face up to 5M baht penalties. 87% public support (highest globally per Ipsos).

AK Party draft bill would amend Law No. 5651 to ban social media for under-15s, with parental controls for ages 15-18. Human Rights Commission accepted supporting report February 2026. Night-time internet restrictions for under-18 also proposed.

law_name: Federal Decree-Law No. 26/2025 On Child Digital Safety (CDS Law)
description: Comprehensive child digital safety law. Prohibits data collection from under-13s without verifiable parental consent. Requires age verification, content filtering, and parental controls for under-18. One-year compliance grace period until January 2027.

law_name: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill (Amendment)
description: UK government will trial social media restrictions on 300 teens alongside consultation on potentially banning under-16s. Online Safety Act (2023) already requires age verification for harmful content from July 2025.

law_name: Kids Off Social Media Act (KOSMA)
description: Federal KOSMA (S.278) passed Senate Commerce Committee February 2025; awaiting full Senate vote. Would ban under-13s and algorithmic feeds for under-17s. 10+ states enacted varying restrictions; some blocked on First Amendment grounds.

law_name: Decree 147/2024/ND-CP
description: Parents must register social media accounts for children under 16 and supervise online activities. Mandatory user authentication on all social media platforms. Not an outright ban; active regulation of minors' access.
Albania banned TikTok for one year (March 2025–Feb 2026) after a teenager fatally stabbed a classmate. Ban lifted Feb 5, 2026 after TikTok agreed to new safety mechanisms. Now in 'monitoring phase.'

law_name: Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024
description: World's first outright ban on social media for under-16s. Covers major platforms. Parents cannot consent on behalf of children. Penalties up to A$49.5 million for platforms.
Three-party government announced March 27, 2026 plan to ban social media for under-14s, accompanied by media literacy programs in schools.
No national social media age ban. Wallonia-Brussels Federation signed EU age verification letter. All three regions have banned smartphones in schools.

law_name: ECA Digital (Digital Statute of the Child and Adolescent)
description: First Latin American dedicated children's online safety law. Under-16 accounts must link to guardians. Bans behavioral advertising and algorithmic profiling of minors. Fines up to 10% of Brazilian revenue.

Liberal Party of Canada convention (April 11, 2026) passed a non-binding grassroots resolution setting 16 as the social media age of majority, placing onus on platforms. PM Carney said it 'merits debate' but has no settled view. No government legislation introduced. Nova Scotia planning under-16 bill. Quebec recommends barring under-14s without parental consent. PIPEDA operative but doesn't restrict social media access.

law_name: Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Cyberspace
description: Comprehensive tiered age restrictions. 'Minor Mode' limits screen time (40 min/day for under-14), blocks usage 10pm–6am, requires age-appropriate content filters. Fines up to 1 million RMB.
PM Babiš voiced support for ban on platforms for under-15s. Vice PM Havlíček confirmed government negotiations with experts. No formal bill introduced.

law_name: Social Media Age Ban Agreement
description: Cross-party agreement (Nov 2025) to ban social media for under-15s, with parental opt-in from 13. 160M kroner allocated. Legislation expected mid-to-late 2026.
Children's Commission processing ADN party proposal to prohibit social media for under-15s. Reform to Children and Adolescents Code. Filed December 2025.
President el-Sissi directed legislation restricting children's social media to combat 'digital chaos.' Parliamentary discussion underway.

law_name: European Parliament Resolution on Protection of Minors Online
description: EP voted 483-92 for non-binding resolution urging minimum age 16. Five EU countries piloting age verification app. GDPR Article 8 already sets default digital consent age of 16.
PM Orpo supports ban for under-15s. Two-thirds of Finns support. Health institute recommends no smartphones for under-13s. School phone ban enacted August 2025.

law_name: Loi interdisant l'accès aux réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans
description: France enacted a law on April 8, 2026 banning social media access for under-15s, effective 2027 (pending EU age verification system). National Assembly passed blanket ban version Jan 26 (130-21); Senate passed a two-tier blacklist version April 1; government announced final reconciled ban April 8. Enforcement from 2027 aligned with EU age verification rollout. Also bans mobile phones in French high schools.
Expert committee study commissioned November 2025 (report due summer 2026). Chancellor Merz supports raising minimum age to 16 for Instagram and TikTok. Joint CDU/SPD proposal expected.

Digital Governance Minister says Greece is 'very close' to banning under-15s. Plans Kids Wallet app for device-level age verification. 80% public support. EU pilot country; Coalition of Digitally Willing member.
Union government considering restricting social media for under-16s by amending IT Intermediary Guidelines. IT minister confirmed active discussions with platforms.

law_name: Child Protection in Digital Space Regulation (PP TUNAS) (Government Regulation No. 17 of 2025)
description: Under-16s 'delayed access' to social media starting March 28, 2026. Under-13s limited to age-specific platforms; 13-16 with parental consent on low-risk services. Tiered by age. Sanctions on platforms.

Government planning MyGovID-based age verification with 2,000-person pilot in Q1 2026. Plans to make child online safety a key EU Council presidency theme. Rejected Australia-style ban in favor of 'incremental' steps.

law_name: Child Social Media Protection Bill
description: Senate bill would restrict social media for under-15s and ban kidfluencers. AGCOM approved age verification regulation April 2025. Class action by MOIGE (3.5M children ages 7-14) pending. Italy piloting EU age verification app.

law_name: Children and Families Agency Working Group (2025)
description: No dedicated social media age ban. Information Distribution Platform Act (April 2025) requires transparency not age bans. Government working group studying options. First municipal smartphone ordinance in Aichi Prefecture.

law_name: Online Safety Act
description: Online Safety Act received royal assent May 2025, effective January 1, 2026. Platforms with 8M+ Malaysian users must implement eKYC age verification using government-issued IDs. Fines up to RM 500,000 and 5 years imprisonment.

law_name: Guidelines for Healthy Screen and Social Media Use
description: Government officially advised against social media for under-15s (June 2025) citing psychological health concerns. Coalition pushing to codify in legislation. Dutch minority government pitched EU minimum age of 15.

Federal government launched consultations with experts, civil society groups, and technology companies in early 2026 on possible social media age restrictions. Digital Secretary Delgado announced proposals expected by June 2026. Jalisco Congress separately studying a local bill to ban social media for under-14s on school grounds. No federal bill introduced.

law_name: Social Media (Age-Restricted Users) Bill
description: Member's bill (Catherine Wedd) modeled on Australia's law. PM Luxon confirmed in government 2026 work program. ACT coalition partner opposes, blocking government bill adoption. Parliamentary inquiry recommended restrictions December 2025.

Nigeria's Data Protection Commission (NDPC) formally launched a government public consultation on March 10, 2026 on whether to introduce age restrictions for social media use, including minimum age requirements, stronger age verification, and increased platform accountability. No bill introduced; consultation phase only.
